assessment: Freeze all six asset/date trajectories for every case before metric reveal. Compare every adaptive case with frozen-reference, fixed-weight controls, its global/context match, both assets and every date. All dates are exposed development data. The ongoing CatBoost scores are excluded and remain sealed; compare that separately completed family before any later promotion.
causality_and_replay: Before revealing any family score, require the frozen-reference control to reproduce original complete p and both decision policies exactly. Verify all rows, labels and clocks; exact integer releases >=decision+5100; prefix invariance when unreleased labels or future expert forecasts change; independent explicit discounted-sum parity; exact repeated and saved-trajectory replay.
context: Normalize the reference p/prior row to sum one. Context is its argmax class times three plus the top-two margin bin [0,.1), [.1,.25), [.25,1]. Margins exactly .1 and .25 enter the higher bin. Nine contexts; original saved forecast_3600 priors are used.
discount: At decision t, S_m(t)=sum_{i:release_i<=t} eta*2^(-(t-decision_i)/(1000*half_life_seconds))*ell_i,m. Apply exponential decay to accumulated state and add each newly released loss exactly once with its original decision age. Do not treat the nominal horizon as the actual release time.
feedback: Full-information delayed supervised feedback: once the exact target quote arrives, all experts losses are observable. This is not a bandit or reinforcement-learning environment. Outcomes with release after the current decision never enter state.
hypothesis: Some complementary expert errors may be predictable from delayed realized losses and the reference confidence context. Test low-dimensional coefficient adaptation without refitting any base learner. The hindsight ceiling is not assumed attainable.
initial_weights: Reference receives 1/2; each of the other eight experts receives 1/16. Uniform-eight control assigns 1/8 to each individual and zero to the reference. All states reset independently per asset/date at the first original noon row.
loss: For expert m and released label y_i, ell_i,m = (min_c pi_train,c / pi_train,y_i) * 1[d_i,m != y_i], in [0,1]. d_i,m is its frozen forecast_3600 hard decision. The fixed historical prior makes this a bounded proxy for class-balanced error; it is not an exact current balanced-risk loss under prior shift.
prediction: Take the arithmetic mixture of the unchanged natural expert posteriors at the current row. Recompute the existing causal forecast_3600 prior policy for this mixture from the same frozen initial prior. Also retain the original registered historical-prior decision control. Mixture probabilities remain normalized; calibration is not guaranteed.

primary_sources.scope: Freund and Schapire 1997 motivates exponential expert weighting; this is not AdaBoost training.
Joulani et al. 2013 motivates treating actual delayed feedback explicitly; the registered procedure is not a replication of their meta-algorithm guarantees.

resources: This is a small coefficient-only study over nine saved forecast vectors, not a substantial base-model fit. Use one CPU thread, sampled RSS below 1 GiB and 60 seconds per asset/date trajectory; first run a bounded full-length synthetic case. It may run alongside the existing two-thread boosting worker only after passing that small resource preflight. Do not change any pinned source or input of the running boosting family.
theory_scope: Classical expert-advice results concern their stated loss/game. Discounting, confidence contexts, delayed feedback, class-prior mismatch and argmax of a probability mixture change that setting. No regret bound or guaranteed balanced-accuracy gain is claimed for this registered finite procedure.
weights: Global weights are softmax(log(initial_weights)-S_global). Mix 95% learned weights with 5% initial weights. Context variant averages this result with the identically floored softmax from only historical rows in the current confidence context. No gate networks or fitted thresholds.
